newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile to cut subsidy for private health insurers.
newsitem.headline: Chile to cut subsidy for private health insurers.

text.p: Chile will scrap a $60 million annual government subsidy to private health insurers because it is no longer necessary, President Eduardo Frei said on Wednesday..

The proposal, made by Frei in his annual speech to Congress, was sure to raise the hackles of health insurance companies, known as Isapres, which say the subsidy allows them to insure indigent and high-risk clients.

"The Isapre system does not require public subsidies for its development...(and) their elimination cannot be delayed," Frei said. "Therefore, I have decided that during the second half of this year, I will send to Congress a bill that eliminates, as of January 1, 1998, that subsidy."
The subsidy amounts to about 25 billion pesos a year, or about $60 million, the president said.

The announcement had been expected by health insurance companies, which said earlier this week that the elimination of the subsidy would force poorer clients to turn to Fonasa, the state insurance scheme, for coverage.

The Isapres Association, a trade group, said the move would send about 370,000 savers and their families, or about a total of a million people, to Fonasa. Government officials later said the association's estimate was highly exaggerated.
